correctness.rationale: Prue–Scrimshaw's subdivision conditions at two particles hold (essential vertices of degree four at edge distance at least one; girth three), including the unordered application. In the two-dimensional discrete model independent exact reconstruction gives (36,126,99) cells, ∂₁∂₂=0, and ∂₂ Smith factors 1^80,2, hence free top homology of rank 18. All triangles are rows or columns; every square alternates the two coordinate directions and is a rectangle. For each triangle three squares in the other two lines are disjoint; permutations of coordinates and the transpose give one orbit of the 18 pairs. The product chains use the sign of any exchange of oriented edge factors. Recomputed mixed-chain Smith factors are 1^16,2,2 and the specified maximal minor is −4. Since the mixed classes are cycles of full rank, their saturation in C₂ is ker ∂₂; the finite quotient is (Z/2)^2, not torsion of H₂. The specified extension unit minor is +1, and independent Smith checks of all nine choices of one row-pair plus one column-pair give 18 unit factors. Equivalently S₃×S₃ acts transitively on these simultaneous choices and preserves the mixed family. value.rationale: The selected tori are the entire natural symmetry orbit of disjoint triangle-square products, not an arbitrary submatrix. Its classes are a rational basis yet miss two integral parity classes, which are supplied by two geometrically distinct types of triangle-pair torus. This sharp invariant answers an integral generation question not settled by the ambient Betti number or general product generation; no general rook-graph formula is required for it to be useful.
